request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grace days are in, and changing the sheet's today now closes overdue periods on its own. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests. After that run I only edited a comment in an endpoint YAML file, so I didn't run it again.

**The setting**
- `grace-days` is a new sheet setting: a whole number of days, 0 or more, or blank for off. It isn't dated. A value that isn't a whole number is refused, and saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED ... key=grace-days value=<days>`.
- The settings form has a new field for it (`setting-grace-days`) and shows the current value (`setting-grace-days-current`). The checks are in `setting/ValidateSetting.java` and `setting/SettingRepository.java`.

**Auto-close**
- I moved the period-closing logic out of `ClosePeriod` into a shared `period/PeriodCloser.java`. Closing by hand and auto-closing now run the same code, so totals come out the same.
- A new step, `period/AutoClosePeriods.java`, runs right after the new today is saved. If grace days are set, it closes every open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, earliest to-date first. Each close writes `PERIOD_CLOSED ... total=<x> auto=yes`, and these lines come before the today change's rollup lines.

**A choice for you:** an auto-close doesn't check the sheet's close permission, so whoever changes today can trigger closes their role couldn't make by hand. I did this so a today change is never refused because of a close the user didn't ask for. If you'd rather auto-close follow the same permission rule as a manual close, that's a small change.
